papers.title: Piercing through the Haze: Characterizing Titan-like terrestrial exoplanets with JWST
papers.abstract: As we enter a new era of using JWST to characterize exoplanet atmospheres, a top priority is defining observational needs and parameters in the search for life on an exoplanet. Although some studies have begun to consider Titan-like exoplanet atmospheres, more work is needed to prepare for the potential discovery and characterization of Titan analogues with JWST and future missions. We explore the effectiveness of exoplanet atmospheric retrieval methodologies on the Cassini/VIMS-IR spectrum of Titan assuming agnostic haze properties and tholin hazes, as well as a self-consistent photochemical model. We compare our retrieved chemical abundances and haze profiles against fiducial values and Cassini/ISS-NAC UV observations and the forward modeled truths. We generalize these findings to a Titan-like exoplanet in the TRAPPIST-1 system and find that JWST-like observations have limited potential to identify features beyond methane in a Titan-like atmosphere, but may be able to identify the presence of the haze to a few hundred kilometers. The diagnostic features which would differentiate between different haze model (scattering) properties are shortward of 1\, and further demonstrate the important role of nUV -- optical observatories in constraining the properties of exoplanet atmospheres. We also find that agnostic priors for the bulk atmosphere can lead to a degeneracy in which a spectrally active gas ( CH₄) is erroneously favored as the dominant atmospheric constituent over a spectrally inactive molecule (N₂).
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) is now reading the atmospheres of planets around other stars, and astronomers want to know what it can and cannot tell us in the search for life. Saturn's moon Titan is a useful model. It has a thick, smoggy, nitrogen-rich atmosphere with orange organic haze, and similar worlds may well exist around other stars. If we find one, we need to know in advance how well we can read its air through all that haze. Haze acts like fog on a car windshield, hiding what lies beneath.

**What They Did**
The team took a real infrared spectrum of Titan, essentially its light split into colors, collected by the Cassini spacecraft. They treated it as if it were a distant exoplanet and ran "retrieval" methods on it. A retrieval works backward from the light to estimate which gases and haze are present. They tried several ways of describing the haze: a flexible "agnostic" approach, a lab-made haze material called tholin, and a detailed model of the chemistry driven by sunlight. They checked the results against what Cassini measured directly and against the known truth. Then they applied the lessons to an imagined Titan-like planet in the TRAPPIST-1 system.

**Key Findings**
JWST-like observations would have limited power to detect anything beyond methane in a Titan-like atmosphere. They might, however, be able to detect that haze is present, down to a few hundred kilometers in altitude. The clues that would tell different haze types apart lie at wavelengths shorter than 1 micron, which is near-ultraviolet and visible light. The team also found a pitfall: when the method assumes little about the main background gas, it can wrongly favor methane, which absorbs light strongly, over nitrogen, which is nearly invisible.

**Looking Forward**
The results suggest that near-ultraviolet and optical observatories will be important partners to JWST for understanding hazy worlds. They also show that the assumptions built into analysis methods matter, and that astronomers should be careful about them when interpreting future observations.

papers.title_tr: Sisin Ötesine Bakmak: JWST ile Titan Benzeri Karasal Ötegezegenlerin Karakterizasyonu
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
James Webb Uzay Teleskobu (JWST) artık başka yıldızların çevresindeki gezegenlerin atmosferlerini inceliyor. Gökbilimciler, yaşam arayışında bu teleskobun neleri söyleyip neleri söyleyemeyeceğini bilmek istiyor. Satürn'ün uydusu Titan bu iş için iyi bir model. Titan'ın, turuncu renkli organik sisle dolu, kalın ve azot bakımından zengin bir atmosferi var. Benzer dünyaların başka yıldızların çevresinde de bulunması mümkün. Böyle bir dünya bulursak, o yoğun sisin arkasındaki havayı ne kadar iyi okuyabileceğimizi önceden bilmemiz gerekir. Sis, bir araba camındaki buğu gibi altındaki her şeyi gizler.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Ekip, Cassini uzay aracının topladığı, Titan'ın ışığının renklerine ayrılmış hâli olan gerçek bir kızılötesi tayfı aldı. Bu tayfı sanki uzaktaki bir ötegezegenden gelmiş gibi ele alıp "geri çatım" (retrieval) yöntemlerini uyguladı. Geri çatım, ışıktan geriye giderek hangi gazların ve ne tür bir sisin bulunduğunu kestirme işlemidir. Sis için birkaç farklı tanım denendi: esnek ve "agnostik" bir yaklaşım, laboratuvarda üretilen tholin adlı sis malzemesi ve güneş ışığının yönlendirdiği kimyayı ayrıntılı biçimde modelleyen bir yaklaşım. Sonuçlar, Cassini'nin doğrudan ölçümleriyle ve bilinen gerçek değerlerle karşılaştırıldı. Ardından çıkarılan dersler, TRAPPIST-1 sistemindeki Titan benzeri varsayımsal bir gezegene uygulandı.

**Ana Bulgular**
JWST benzeri gözlemler, Titan benzeri bir atmosferde metanın ötesindeki özellikleri belirlemekte sınırlı kalıyor. Ancak sisin varlığını, birkaç yüz kilometreye kadar olan yüksekliklerde fark edebilirler. Farklı sis türlerini birbirinden ayıracak ipuçları ise 1 mikrondan kısa dalga boylarında, yani yakın morötesi ve görünür ışıkta yer alıyor. Ekip bir tuzak da buldu: Yöntem ana gaz hakkında çok az varsayımda bulunduğunda, ışığı güçlü biçimde soğuran metanı, neredeyse görünmez olan azota tercih ederek yanlış sonuca varabiliyor.

**İleriye Bakış**
Bu sonuçlar, sisli dünyaları anlamak için yakın morötesi ve optik gözlemevlerinin JWST'ye önemli birer ortak olacağını gösteriyor. Ayrıca analiz yöntemlerine yerleştirilen varsayımların önemli olduğunu ve gelecekteki gözlemler yorumlanırken bunlara dikkat edilmesi gerektiğini ortaya koyuyor.

papers.title: Reflation: redox-driven atmospheric inflation as tracer of super-Earth geochemistry
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that the redox-sensitivity of mantle outgassing can trigger transient episodes of atmospheric re-inflation in highly irradiated and geochemically-reduced super-Earths, a mechanism we term reflation. Mantle redox governs the outgassing and speciation of CHONS volatiles, setting the background secondary atmospheric composition during extended photoevaporation at highly irradiated conditions. Using simulations of the coupled atmosphere-interior evolution of irradiated super-Earths, we illustrate that reduced mantles close to the iron-wustite buffer initially produce CO-dominated atmospheres. Hydrodynamic escape continuously removes volatiles while outgassing from the melt replenishes the atmosphere with H2, converted from H2O dissolved in the underlying magma ocean. This leads to a late-stage transition from C- to H-dominated gas that transiently re-inflates super-Earth atmospheres and decreases their bulk densities by up to 60\% between several hundreds of Myr to Gyr after their formation, prior to complete atmospheric erosion by photoevaporation. In contrast, oxidised mantles, closer to Earth-like geochemistry, strongly buffer their atmospheric composition while exposed to hydrodynamic escape, producing monotonic radius deflation. Reflation events are triggered by geochemically-reduced mantles, intermediate escape efficiencies, high irradiation, and initial water inventories 5 Earth oceans. This redox-dependent evolutionary divergence hinges on the sensitive feedback between interior and atmospheric evolution serving as a potential tracer of historical geochemical state. Population-level reflation signatures of close-in super-Earths may thus serve as tracers of interior geochemistry and formation conditions.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Many of the planets we find are "super-Earths," rocky worlds somewhat larger than our own. Some orbit so close to their stars that intense radiation slowly strips away their atmospheres, much like a hot wind drying a puddle. This study suggests the way that stripping unfolds depends on the chemistry of the planet's rocky interior. That means the size and density of a planet today could be a clue to what is happening deep inside it, which we cannot observe directly.

**What They Did**
The researchers built computer simulations that link a planet's interior with its atmosphere over billions of years. They modelled hot, close-in super-Earths with magma oceans, molten rock that can hold dissolved gases and release them. The key variable was "redox," a measure of how oxygen-rich or oxygen-poor the mantle is. They compared reduced (oxygen-poor) mantles near a benchmark called the iron-wüstite buffer with oxidised mantles closer to Earth's.

**Key Findings**
Reduced mantles first produce atmospheres dominated by carbon monoxide. As starlight-driven escape removes gas, the magma ocean keeps replenishing the atmosphere with hydrogen made from dissolved water. The atmosphere then shifts from carbon-dominated to hydrogen-dominated and puffs back up, a process the authors call "reflation." This can lower the planet's bulk density by up to 60%, hundreds of millions to billions of years after formation, before the atmosphere is finally lost completely. Oxidised mantles instead keep their atmospheric makeup steady, and the planet simply shrinks over time. Reflation needs a reduced mantle, a moderate escape efficiency, strong irradiation, and a starting water supply of at least about 5 Earth oceans.

**Looking Forward**
If reflation really happens, a population of close-in super-Earths might show telltale patterns in their sizes and densities at certain ages. Astronomers could then use these patterns to infer the chemistry of planetary interiors and the conditions under which the planets formed. This is a theoretical prediction from simulations, and it will need to be tested against observations.

papers.title_tr: Yeniden şişme (Reflation): Süper-Dünyaların jeokimyasının izleyicisi olarak redoks kaynaklı atmosferik şişme
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Keşfettiğimiz gezegenlerin çoğu "süper-Dünya"dır; yani bizimkinden biraz daha büyük kayaç gezegenlerdir. Bazıları yıldızlarına o kadar yakın döner ki yoğun radyasyon atmosferlerini yavaş yavaş sıyırıp götürür; tıpkı sıcak bir rüzgârın bir su birikintisini kurutması gibi. Bu çalışma, bu sıyrılmanın nasıl ilerlediğinin gezegenin kayaç iç kısmının kimyasına bağlı olduğunu öne sürüyor. Yani bir gezegenin bugünkü boyutu ve yoğunluğu, doğrudan gözlemleyemediğimiz derin iç yapısı hakkında ipucu verebilir.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Araştırmacılar, bir gezegenin iç kısmını ve atmosferini milyarlarca yıl boyunca birbirine bağlayan bilgisayar simülasyonları kurdu. Magma okyanuslarına sahip, sıcak ve yıldızına yakın süper-Dünyaları modellediler. Magma okyanusu, içinde gaz çözebilen ve sonra bu gazları dışarı verebilen erimiş kayaçtır. Temel değişken "redoks"tu; yani manto ne kadar oksijen bakımından zengin ya da fakir. Demir-vüstit tamponu denen bir ölçüt civarındaki indirgenmiş (oksijence fakir) mantoları, Dünya'nınkine daha yakın yükseltgenmiş mantolarla karşılaştırdılar.

**Ana Bulgular**
İndirgenmiş mantolar önce karbon monoksit ağırlıklı atmosferler üretiyor. Yıldız ışınımının tetiklediği kaçış gazı uzaklaştırdıkça, magma okyanusu çözünmüş sudan üretilen hidrojenle atmosferi yeniden dolduruyor. Atmosfer karbon ağırlıklıdan hidrojen ağırlıklıya geçiyor ve yeniden şişiyor; yazarlar bu sürece "reflation" (yeniden şişme) diyor. Bu durum, gezegenin ortalama yoğunluğunu oluşumundan yüz milyonlarca ila milyarlarca yıl sonra, atmosfer tümüyle kaybolmadan önce, %60'a varan oranda azaltabiliyor. Yükseltgenmiş mantolar ise atmosfer bileşimini dengede tutuyor ve gezegen zamanla yalnızca küçülüyor. Yeniden şişme için indirgenmiş bir manto, orta düzeyde kaçış verimi, güçlü ışınım ve yaklaşık 5 Dünya okyanusu veya daha fazla başlangıç su miktarı gerekiyor.

**İleriye Bakış**
Yeniden şişme gerçekten oluyorsa, yıldızlarına yakın süper-Dünya topluluğu belirli yaşlarda boyut ve yoğunluklarında ayırt edici örüntüler gösterebilir. Gökbilimciler bu örüntülerle gezegen iç kısımlarının kimyasını ve gezegenlerin oluştuğu koşulları çıkarabilir. Bu, simülasyonlara dayanan kuramsal bir öngörüdür ve gözlemlerle sınanması gerekecektir.

papers.title: Cradle of Life: From the Formation of Stars to Habitable Worlds with the SKAO
papers.abstract: This chapter provides an overview of the different science cases covered by the "Cradle of Life" working group, which aims to leverage the capabilities of the Square Kilometre Array Observatory (SKAO) to trace the physical and chemical pathways toward stars and planets formation, how such stars impact their planets, and whether life could exist in such conditions. At its highest frequencies, the SKAO will probe the earliest stages of the raw material fuelling planet formation, while enabling deep, unprecedented searches for prebiotic molecules both in high-mass and solar-type protostars. Concurrently, the lowest frequencies will be deployed to detect and characterize exoplanetary magnetic fields via their auroral radio emission, and the type of space weather a planet experiences from its host star. Across the entire frequency range, the SKA telescopes will conduct systematic searches of technosignatures. Together, these high-impact research areas establish a comprehensive roadmap for the SKAO to uncover the origins of life in the universe.
authors: the Cradle of Life working group
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Humans have long asked where stars, planets, and life come from. The answer is a long chain of events, from a cold cloud of gas and dust, to a newborn star, to planets, and possibly to living worlds. Each link is hard to study because the early stages are hidden inside thick dust that blocks ordinary visible light. Radio waves can pass through that dust, much as a radio signal can reach you inside a building where you cannot see the transmitter. This paper explains how a new radio observatory could help connect the whole chain.

**What They Did**
The authors belong to the "Cradle of Life" working group, a team of scientists planning research for the Square Kilometre Array Observatory (SKAO). The SKAO is a very large network of radio telescopes. This chapter does not report new observations. It is an overview of the science the group hopes to do and how the telescope's different radio frequencies suit different questions.

**Key Findings**
Because this is a planning document, the "findings" are the proposed research goals. At its highest frequencies, the SKAO is expected to study the earliest stages of the raw material that feeds planet formation. It will also search deeply for prebiotic molecules, the chemical building blocks that could lead to life, around both massive young stars and young Sun-like stars. At its lowest frequencies, it is expected to detect radio signals from auroras on planets outside our Solar System. Auroras are the radio-wave cousins of Earth's northern lights, and they could reveal whether those planets have magnetic fields. The same observations could show what kind of "space weather," meaning stormy outflows of particles and radiation, a planet experiences from its star. Across all frequencies, the telescopes will also systematically search for technosignatures, which are possible signs of technology elsewhere.

**Looking Forward**
The chapter sets out a roadmap rather than results. If the SKAO delivers what is planned, astronomers could follow the story of life's ingredients from the birth of stars to planets that might be habitable, all with one facility. Whether any of these searches finds something remains to be seen.

The SKAO is a very large network of radio telescopes. This chapter does not report new observations. It is an overview of the science the group hopes to do and how the telescope's different radio frequencies suit different questions.

Key Findings

Because this is a planning document, the "findings" are the proposed research goals. At its highest frequencies, the SKAO is expected to study the earliest stages of the raw material that feeds planet formation. It will also search deeply for prebiotic molecules, the chemical building blocks that could lead to life, around both massive young stars and young Sun-like stars. At its lowest frequencies, it is expected to detect radio signals from auroras on planets outside our Solar System. Auroras are the radio-wave cousins of Earth's northern lights, and they could reveal whether those planets have magnetic fields. The same observations could show what kind of "space weather," meaning stormy outflows of particles and radiation, a planet experiences from its star. Across all frequencies, the telescopes will also systematically search for technosignatures, which are possible signs of technology elsewhere.

The chapter sets out a roadmap rather than results. If the SKAO delivers what is planned, astronomers could follow the story of life's ingredients from the birth of stars to planets that might be habitable, all with one facility. Whether any of these searches finds something remains to be seen.

Zincirin her halkasını incelemek zor, çünkü en erken evreler sıradan görünür ışığı engelleyen yoğun tozun içinde gizleniyor. papers.title: Photometric Variability and Rotation of Beta Pictoris b from JWST NIRCam Coronagraphic Imaging
papers.abstract: We report the detection of photometric variability in the directly imaged super-Jupiter β Pictoris b. Using JWST NIRCam dual-band coronagraphic imaging, we conducted a 16-hour continuous photometric monitoring campaign in the F210M and F410M filters. We developed and validated a time-series photometry framework that combines PSF subtraction, principal component analysis for systematic noise removal, and injection-and-recovery tests to confirm signal fidelity. Both light curves show consistent sinusoidal variability at 5σ and 5σ significance in the F210M and F410M bands, respectively. A joint sinusoidal fit yields a rotation period of P rₒt = 9.00 ± 0.13 hr and variability amplitudes of 0.85 ± 0.07\% and 0.89 ± 0.04\% in F210M and F410M, respectively. The near-identical amplitudes and periods in both bands confirm a common astrophysical origin in a heterogeneous atmosphere. Combining P rₒt with the previously measured projected rotational velocity, we constrain the line-of-sight spin axis inclination of β Pic b. The result favors an equator-on viewing geometry, consistent with line-of-sight spin-orbit alignment: the planetary spin axis, orbital plane, debris disk, and stellar equator are all mutually aligned. This stands in sharp contrast to the large obliquities of wide-separation companions that are likely formed via gravitational fragmentation. Together with the system's young age, this observation provides independent dynamical evidence that β Pic b formed via core accretion. This result constitutes the first detection of rotational modulation in a close-in, high-contrast exoplanet that likely formed via core accretion, demonstrating that time-series coronagraphic imaging with JWST opens a powerful new window onto the rotation, atmospheric dynamics, and spin-orbit architecture of this population.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
How a planet spins can reveal how it was born. Giant planets built from the bottom up, by a rocky core gathering gas (called core accretion), are expected to spin in step with the disk of gas and dust around their star. Distant companions that form more like stars, when a collapsing cloud breaks into pieces, often end up tilted at odd angles. Beta Pictoris b is a young "super-Jupiter," a planet more massive than Jupiter. Its spin is therefore a clue to its origin.

**What They Did**
The team used the James Webb Space Telescope's NIRCam camera with a coronagraph, a device that blocks starlight much as you might hold up your hand to hide the Sun and see a streetlamp. They watched Beta Pictoris b for 16 hours without a break, in two infrared colors (the F210M and F410M filters). They built a method to subtract the star's glare and used principal component analysis, a statistical technique that finds and removes wobbles caused by the instrument rather than the planet. They also checked the method by adding fake signals to the data and seeing whether they could recover them.

**Key Findings**
In both colors, the planet's brightness rose and fell in a smooth, repeating wave, detected at roughly 5 sigma significance (a high statistical confidence) in each. The pattern repeats every 9.00 ± 0.13 hours, which is the planet's rotation period, or the length of its day. The brightness changes by about 0.85% in one color and 0.89% in the other. Because the period and size of the changes match in both colors, the authors conclude the signal comes from the planet itself, probably from an uneven atmosphere. Combining the period with an earlier measurement of how fast the planet's surface moves, they find the planet is most likely viewed from its equator. This means its spin axis lines up with its orbit, the surrounding debris disk, and the star's equator. That contrasts with the large tilts seen in wide-orbit companions thought to form by fragmentation. Together with the system's young age, this supports formation by core accretion.

**Looking Forward**
This is the first detection of rotational brightness changes in a close-in, directly imaged planet that likely formed by core accretion. It shows that JWST time-series imaging can probe the spins, weather, and alignment of such worlds.

papers.title_tr: Beta Pictoris b'nin Fotometrik Değişkenliği ve Dönmesi: JWST NIRCam Koronagrafik Görüntülemesinden Sonuçlar
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Bir gezegenin nasıl döndüğü, nasıl doğduğunu ortaya çıkarabilir. Kayalık bir çekirdeğin gaz toplamasıyla, yani çekirdek birikimi (core accretion) yoluyla oluşan dev gezegenlerin, yıldızlarını çevreleyen gaz ve toz diskiyle uyumlu biçimde dönmesi beklenir. Çökmekte olan bir bulutun parçalanmasıyla, yıldızlara daha çok benzer biçimde oluşan uzak eşlerse çoğu zaman garip açılarla eğik kalır. Beta Pictoris b, genç bir "süper-Jüpiter"dir, yani Jüpiter'den daha kütleli bir gezegendir. Dolayısıyla dönmesi, kökenine dair önemli bir ipucu sunar.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Ekip, James Webb Uzay Teleskobu'nun NIRCam kamerasını bir koronagrafla birlikte kullandı. Koronagraf, bir sokak lambasını görebilmek için Güneş'i elinizle kapatmanıza benzer biçimde yıldız ışığını engelleyen bir aygıttır. Beta Pictoris b'yi iki kızılötesi renkte (F210M ve F410M filtreleri) 16 saat boyunca kesintisiz izlediler. Yıldızın parlamasını çıkarmak için bir yöntem geliştirdiler ve asıl sinyali gezegenden değil de aygıttan kaynaklanan dalgalanmalardan ayırmak için temel bileşen analizi (principal component analysis) denilen istatistiksel tekniği kullandılar. Yöntemi, verilere sahte sinyaller ekleyip bunları geri çıkarıp çıkaramadıklarına bakarak da sınadılar.

**Ana Bulgular**
Her iki renkte de gezegenin parlaklığı düzgün ve tekrarlayan bir dalga biçiminde arttı ve azaldı. Bu sinyal, her birinde yaklaşık 5 sigma anlamlılıkta (yüksek bir istatistiksel güven düzeyi) saptandı. Desen her 9,00 ± 0,13 saatte bir tekrarlanıyor; bu, gezegenin dönme periyodu, yani bir günün uzunluğudur. Parlaklık bir renkte yaklaşık %0,85, diğerinde %0,89 değişiyor. Periyot ve değişim büyüklüğü iki renkte de uyumlu olduğundan yazarlar sinyalin gezegenin kendisinden, büyük olasılıkla homojen olmayan bir atmosferden geldiği sonucuna varıyor. Dönme periyodunu, gezegen yüzeyinin ne kadar hızlı hareket ettiğine dair daha önceki bir ölçümle birleştirdiklerinde, gezegenin büyük olasılıkla ekvatorundan görüldüğünü buluyorlar. Bu, dönme ekseninin yörüngesi, çevresindeki enkaz diski ve yıldızın ekvatoruyla hizalı olduğu anlamına geliyor. Bu durum, parçalanma yoluyla oluştuğu düşünülen geniş yörüngeli eşlerde görülen büyük eğikliklerle tezat oluşturuyor. Sistemin genç yaşıyla birlikte bu sonuç, çekirdek birikimiyle oluşum fikrini destekliyor.

**İleriye Bakış**
Bu, büyük olasılıkla çekirdek birikimiyle oluşmuş, yıldızına yakın ve doğrudan görüntülenmiş bir gezegende dönmeye bağlı parlaklık değişimlerinin ilk saptanmasıdır. JWST ile yapılan zaman serisi görüntülemenin, bu tür dünyaların dönmesini, havasını ve hizalanmasını inceleyebileceğini gösteriyor.

papers.title: SaNDi-SHoP: Searching for Satellites'N'Disks with a Star-Hopping Program II. Spectrophotometric analysis and orbital monitoring of directly imaged companions
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, advances in high-contrast imaging instrumentation, coupled with extreme adaptive optics systems, have enabled the discovery of tens of planets and brown dwarfs orbiting at wide separations from their host stars (a larger than 10 au). The existence of companions at these separations challenges current planet-formation paradigms, highlighting the importance of high-contrast imaging as the only technique capable of directly probing this region of planetary systems. In this paper, we present a survey of thirteen planets and brown dwarfs observed with VLT/SPHERE between June 2023 and July 2025. These data provide updated photometry in the 1.0-1.7 micron range and new high-precision astrometry, enabling tighter constraints on their orbital properties. We used the IRDIS subsystem to acquire dual-band H2H3 images (H2 = 1.593 microns, H3 = 1.667 microns) for all companions in our sample. For the three objects located within the IFS field of view (GQ Lup B, PZ Tel B, and HD 984 B), we additionally obtained low-resolution (R 50) near-infrared (0.96-1.34 micron) spectra. We combined our new astrometric measurements with those available in the literature to derive updated orbital solutions. The orbital fitting was performed using the orbitize! Python package. For CT Cha b, HIP 78530 B, HIP 64892 B, and RX J1609.5-2105 b, this work provides the first orbital solutions to date. We derived new photometry for all objects, which, when compared with field dwarfs in color-magnitude diagrams, indicates spectral types ranging from mid-M to mid-L. For the companions observed with IFS, their spectra are best matched by those of M6-M8.5 field dwarfs. Our updated orbital fits provide tighter constraints for nearly all companions and are consistent with non-circular orbits in all cases, potentially disfavoring core-accretion formation within their circumstellar disks.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Our own solar system has planets that orbit fairly close to the Sun, with Neptune, the farthest, about 30 times the Earth–Sun distance away. Yet astronomers have now found planets and brown dwarfs (objects too big to be planets but too small to be true stars) circling their stars at more than 10 times that Earth–Sun distance. Some sit much farther out. Their existence is a puzzle, because the leading theory of planet building, which starts with small rocky seeds growing inside a disk of gas and dust, struggles to explain worlds that far out. Direct imaging, which takes actual pictures of these faint companions next to their dazzling stars, is the only technique that can study this outer region.

**What They Did**
The team used the SPHERE instrument on the Very Large Telescope in Chile. Its adaptive optics system corrects for atmospheric blur, and it blocks starlight so faint companions show up. Between June 2023 and July 2025 they observed thirteen planets and brown dwarfs. They took pictures in two near-infrared colors for every object. For three of them (GQ Lup B, PZ Tel B and HD 984 B) they also captured low-resolution spectra, which split light into its component colors. They then combined their new position measurements with older ones and fit orbits using a software package called orbitize!.

**Key Findings**
For CT Cha b, HIP 78530 B, HIP 64892 B and RX J1609.5-2105 b, this is the first orbital solution ever calculated. Based on their brightness and color, the companions resemble stars and brown dwarfs of spectral types from mid-M to mid-L. The three objects with spectra best match M6 to M8.5 dwarfs. For nearly all objects, the orbit estimates became tighter, and every orbit looks non-circular, meaning stretched into an oval. That pattern could argue against the idea that these companions formed by core accretion, the slow seed-growing process, inside their stars' disks.

**Looking Forward**
Continued monitoring will map more of each orbit and sharpen these shapes. That should help reveal whether such distant companions are scaled-up planets or more like failed stars.

papers.title: Revisiting TOI-4438 and TOI-442 planetary systems with new observations from SPIRou and TESS
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive re-analysis of two star-planet systems: TOI-4438, an M3.5V star hosting a mini-Neptune in a 7.4-day orbit, and TOI-442, an M1V star with a 4-day period planet located within the hot Neptune desert. Both systems were originally identified as transiting planet candidates by TESS and subsequently validated through the radial velocity (RV) method. Our work incorporates new TESS transit data and high-resolution spectroscopy from the SPIRou near-infrared spectropolarimeter. We detect a persistent and relatively strong Zeeman signature in TOI-442, while TOI-4438 exhibits weaker and intermittent magnetic activity, and we infer the stellar rotation periods of both stars from the variability of the longitudinal magnetic field. We jointly fit photometry and RV models for each system. For TOI-4438\,b we combine archival CARMENES data with 81 SPIRou observations and five TESS sectors. This yields a refined planetary mass of M ₚ = 4.11⁺⁰.⁴⁰₋₀.₃₈\,M⊕ and a radius of R ₚ = 2.40⁺⁰.⁰⁹₋₀.₁₀\,R⊕, consistent with the previous estimate within 1.1σ while improving by 53\% the precision on the mass and 22\% on the radius. For TOI-442\,b, we add 29 SPIRou RV measurements to an extensive archival dataset, significantly extending the temporal baseline. With a new TESS sector, we tighten the mass to M ₚ = 28.38⁺⁰.⁷⁷₋₀.₇₃\,M⊕ and radius to R ₚ = 4.25⁺⁰.¹⁰₋₀.₀₈\,R⊕, which agrees to the previous values within 1.5σ and improves the precisions by 46\% and 67\% respectively. We find no clear signs of additional planets in the available RV data, although we detect a single-transit event in the TOI-4438 light curve. We compare various RV models and find that those accounting for stellar variability-induced signals yield improved constraints on the planetary parameters.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Most planets beyond our solar system are far too distant to photograph, so astronomers have to weigh and measure them indirectly. A planet's mass and size reveal whether it is rocky, gassy, or something in between. Small, cool stars called red dwarfs are good places to hunt for planets, but they are also magnetically active. Their flickering and spots can mimic or hide a planet's signal. Getting more precise measurements for these systems helps us understand what kinds of worlds exist, including some in a so-called "hot Neptune desert," where medium-sized planets very close to their stars are surprisingly rare.

**What They Did**
The team revisited two planetary systems, TOI-4438 and TOI-442, first spotted by TESS (the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite). TESS watches for tiny dips in starlight when a planet crosses in front of its star. The researchers added new TESS data and new measurements from SPIRou, an instrument that spreads infrared starlight into fine detail. It can track the small back-and-forth wobble a planet's gravity causes in its star, and it can also detect the star's magnetic field. For TOI-4438 they combined 81 SPIRou observations with older data from an instrument called CARMENES and five TESS sectors. For TOI-442 they added 29 SPIRou measurements to a large existing dataset and one new TESS sector. They also used changes in the stars' magnetic fields to estimate how fast each star spins, and they compared several ways of modeling the stars' own variability.

**Key Findings**
TOI-4438 b has a mass of about 4.11 Earth masses and a radius of about 2.40 Earth radii. That is consistent with earlier estimates, but the mass is now 53% more precise and the radius 22% more precise. TOI-442 b, a planet in the hot Neptune desert, has a mass of about 28.38 Earth masses and a radius of about 4.25 Earth radii. Its mass is 46% more precise and its radius 67% more precise. TOI-442 shows a strong, persistent magnetic signal, while TOI-4438's is weaker and comes and goes. The team found no clear sign of additional planets in the wobble data, but they did spot a single transit-like dip in TOI-4438's light. Models that account for the star's own variability gave better constraints on the planets.

**Looking Forward**
The lone transit event in TOI-4438 is a tantalizing lead that would need further observation to understand. More broadly, the work shows that carefully modeling a star's magnetic activity helps astronomers measure small planets more reliably.

papers.title_tr: TOI-4438 ve TOI-442 Gezegen Sistemlerinin SPIRou ve TESS'ten Yeni Gözlemlerle Yeniden İncelenmesi
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Güneş Sistemi'nin dışındaki gezegenlerin çoğu fotoğraflanamayacak kadar uzaktır. Bu yüzden gökbilimciler onları dolaylı yollarla tartar ve ölçer. Bir gezegenin kütlesi ve boyutu, onun kayalık mı, gazlı mı yoksa ikisinin arasında bir yapıda mı olduğunu gösterir. Kırmızı cüce denen küçük ve soğuk yıldızlar gezegen avı için elverişli yerlerdir, ancak manyetik olarak da çok etkindirler. Titreşimleri ve lekeleri bir gezegenin sinyalini taklit edebilir ya da gizleyebilir. Bu sistemler için daha kesin ölçümler elde etmek, ne tür dünyaların var olduğunu anlamamıza yardımcı olur. Buna, orta boyutlu gezegenlerin yıldızlarına çok yakın yörüngelerde şaşırtıcı biçimde nadir görüldüğü "sıcak Neptün çölü" denen bölgedeki dünyalar da dahildir.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Ekip, ilk kez TESS (Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite) tarafından fark edilen iki gezegen sistemini, TOI-4438 ve TOI-442'yi yeniden inceledi. TESS, bir gezegen yıldızının önünden geçerken yıldız ışığındaki çok küçük azalmaları arar. Araştırmacılar yeni TESS verileri ile SPIRou'dan gelen yeni ölçümleri eklediler. SPIRou, kızılötesi yıldız ışığını ince ayrıntılara ayıran bir araçtır. Bir gezegenin kütleçekiminin yıldızında yarattığı küçük ileri-geri salınımı izleyebilir ve yıldızın manyetik alanını da algılayabilir. TOI-4438 için 81 SPIRou gözlemini, CARMENES adlı bir araçtan gelen eski verilerle ve beş TESS gözlem bölümüyle birleştirdiler. TOI-442 için ise mevcut büyük bir veri kümesine 29 SPIRou ölçümü ve bir yeni TESS bölümü eklediler. Ayrıca yıldızların manyetik alanlarındaki değişimlerden her yıldızın ne kadar hızlı döndüğünü tahmin ettiler ve yıldızların kendi değişkenliğini modellemenin çeşitli yollarını karşılaştırdılar.

**Ana Bulgular**
TOI-4438 b'nin kütlesi yaklaşık 4,11 Dünya kütlesi, yarıçapı ise yaklaşık 2,40 Dünya yarıçapıdır. Bu değerler önceki tahminlerle uyumludur, ancak kütle ölçümü artık %53, yarıçap ölçümü ise %22 daha kesindir. Sıcak Neptün çölünde yer alan TOI-442 b'nin kütlesi yaklaşık 28,38 Dünya kütlesi, yarıçapı yaklaşık 4,25 Dünya yarıçapıdır. Kütlesi %46, yarıçapı %67 daha kesin hale gelmiştir. TOI-442 güçlü ve kalıcı bir manyetik sinyal gösterirken, TOI-4438'in sinyali daha zayıftır ve gelip gitmektedir. Ekip, salınım verilerinde ek gezegenlere dair net bir iz bulamadı, ancak TOI-4438'in ışık eğrisinde tek bir geçişe benzeyen düşüş tespit etti. Yıldızın kendi değişkenliğini hesaba katan modeller, gezegenler hakkında daha iyi kısıtlamalar sağladı.

**İleriye Bakış**
TOI-4438'deki tek geçiş olayı ilgi çekici bir ipucudur, ancak anlaşılması için başka gözlemler gerekir. Daha genel olarak bu çalışma, bir yıldızın manyetik etkinliğini dikkatle modellemenin küçük gezegenleri daha güvenilir ölçmeye yardımcı olduğunu gösteriyor.

papers.title: Growing Planets Produce Extreme Dust Signatures
papers.abstract: Collisions between planetary bodies are essential to the assembly of rocky planets like the Earth, but they are extremely difficult to observe. We therefore rely on indirect signatures of planetary impacts such as extreme debris disks - bright infrared excesses around other stars. Extreme debris disks are thought to be the result of energetic collisions that ejected large amounts of vaporized rock which rapidly condensed into mm- or cm-sized dust. However, previously there has been no clear way to relate the observed mass of dust to the collision that produced it. Here, we show that the colliding bodies required are orders of magnitude more massive than the mass of dust observed. We find that more massive extreme debris disks require proportionally larger colliding bodies. As a consequence, the most massive observed extreme debris disks require collisions of Mars- to Earth-mass bodies. Extreme debris disks thus reveal the ongoing formation of rocky planets comparable in size to the rocky planets of our own solar system.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Rocky planets like Earth were built through violent collisions between smaller bodies. Imagine a cosmic demolition derby lasting millions of years. These crashes are almost impossible to watch directly, because they are rare, brief and happen around distant stars. Astronomers therefore look for indirect clues. One of the best is the "extreme debris disk": a ring of dust around a star that glows so brightly in infrared light (heat radiation our eyes cannot see) that it hints at a recent huge smash-up. Until now, nobody had a clear way to work backward from the amount of dust seen to the size of the collision that made it.

**What They Did**
The researchers tackled that missing link. Current thinking holds that the energetic impacts behind these disks vaporize rock, and the vapor quickly condenses into dust grains the size of a millimeter or a centimeter, much like steam turning into water droplets. The team worked out what colliding bodies would be needed to produce the amount of dust astronomers actually observe.

**Key Findings**
The colliding bodies must be orders of magnitude more massive than the dust itself. In other words, the dust we see is only a small leftover fraction of the material involved. The team also found that disks with more dust require proportionally bigger colliders. As a result, the most massive extreme debris disks observed so far point to collisions between bodies with masses between that of Mars and that of Earth. These disks therefore appear to reveal rocky planets still being assembled, comparable in size to the rocky planets in our own solar system.

**Looking Forward**
This result turns dusty glows into a kind of scale for weighing otherwise invisible collisions, offering a new way to study how rocky planets form. The abstract does not describe specific follow-up observations, but the approach suggests that extreme debris disks could serve as markers of Earth- and Mars-scale planets in the making around other stars.

These disks therefore appear to reveal rocky planets still being assembled, comparable in size to the rocky planets in our own solar system.

Looking Forward

This result turns dusty glows into a kind of scale for weighing otherwise invisible collisions, offering a new way to study how rocky planets form. The abstract does not describe specific follow-up observations, but the approach suggests that extreme debris disks could serve as markers of Earth- and Mars-scale planets in the making around other stars.

papers.title_tr: Büyüyen Gezegenler Aşırı Toz İmzaları Üretiyor
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Dünya gibi kayaç gezegenler, daha küçük cisimlerin şiddetli çarpışmalarıyla oluştu. Bunu milyonlarca yıl süren kozmik bir çarpışan arabalar yarışı gibi düşünebilirsiniz. Bu çarpışmaları doğrudan gözlemlemek neredeyse imkânsızdır; çünkü nadirdirler, çok kısa sürerler ve uzak yıldızların çevresinde gerçekleşirler. Bu yüzden gökbilimciler dolaylı ipuçları arar. En iyi ipuçlarından biri "aşırı enkaz diski"dir: bir yıldızın çevresindeki, kızılötesi ışıkta (gözlerimizin göremediği ısı ışınımında) o kadar parlak görünen bir toz halkasıdır ki yakın zamanda büyük bir çarpışma yaşandığını düşündürür. Şimdiye kadar, gözlenen toz miktarından yola çıkarak onu üreten çarpışmanın büyüklüğüne ulaşmanın net bir yolu yoktu.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Araştırmacılar bu eksik halkayı tamamlamaya çalıştı. Güncel görüşe göre bu disklerin ardındaki enerjik çarpışmalar kayayı buharlaştırır ve bu buhar, tıpkı su buharının damlacıklara dönüşmesi gibi, hızla milimetre ya da santimetre boyutunda toz tanecikleri halinde yoğunlaşır. Ekip, gökbilimcilerin gözlediği toz miktarını üretmek için nasıl çarpışan cisimlerin gerektiğini hesapladı.

**Ana Bulgular**
Çarpışan cisimlerin kütlesi, tozun kütlesinden birkaç büyüklük mertebesi daha fazla olmalıdır. Yani gördüğümüz toz, çarpışmaya katılan malzemenin yalnızca küçük bir artığıdır. Ekip ayrıca daha fazla toz içeren disklerin orantılı olarak daha büyük çarpışan cisimler gerektirdiğini buldu. Sonuç olarak, bugüne dek gözlenen en kütleli aşırı enkaz diskleri, kütleleri Mars ile Dünya arasında değişen cisimlerin çarpışmalarına işaret ediyor. Dolayısıyla bu diskler, kendi Güneş Sistemimizdeki kayaç gezegenlerle kıyaslanabilir büyüklükte, hâlâ oluşmakta olan kayaç gezegenleri ortaya koyuyor gibi görünüyor.

**İleriye Bakış**
Bu sonuç, tozlu parıltıları, görünmeyen çarpışmaları tartmaya yarayan bir ölçeğe dönüştürerek kayaç gezegenlerin nasıl oluştuğunu incelemek için yeni bir yol sunuyor. Özette belirli takip gözlemlerinden söz edilmiyor; ancak bu yaklaşım, aşırı enkaz disklerinin diğer yıldızların çevresinde oluşmakta olan Dünya ve Mars ölçeğindeki gezegenlerin işaretçisi olabileceğini düşündürüyor.
